Q: How to cache POST requests in Python A:

By default requests-cache only caches GET requests because POST requests are considered non-idempotent meaning they can produce different results or side effects each time, so caching them is not standard behavior.

To fix this, explicitly include POST in the list of allowable methods when creating your CachedSession. That tells the library to cache POST responses just like GET requests.

Just note that you should only cache POST requests if you are certain the same input always returns the same response, otherwise you risk getting stale or incorrect cached data.

Q: How to use better OOP for a Huffman Compressor A:

The encoder does not need the tree (as you yourself point out). For basic (non-canonical Huffman) the decoder does need the tree. Side-stepping the issue of communicating the encoding itself to the decoder, the encoder needs a table of Huffman codes by input symbol and a corresponding length for each code. There are several ways you could implement that. A straight-forward approach is to use strings for the code table. Converting to bits, either as the string codes are emitted into a buffer, or as a single final step, is not hard to do.
